title: Regional Launch Corridor & Capacity Sprintmap (Runtime / Console / API)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: produce an operational playbook and sprint-aligned timeline that coordinates Runtime, Console, and API teams for staggered regional launches. This ticket covers the draft sprintmap, capacity reservation lanes, canary cohorts, blackout windows, cross-team cutover checklist, rollback criteria, and owner assignments. Goal is to reduce post-launch incidents by 50% and keep token-cost and latency SLOs within agreed thresholds during regional ramps.
acceptance_criteria: Consolidated sprintmap covering preflight, canary, ramp and scale phases with explicit owners for each task
Capacity reservation lanes (baseline + burst) defined per region and approved by infra finance
Observability gating: perf dashboards and synthetic checks wired to release pipeline with alert thresholds
Runbook with rollback triggers and postmortem checklist drafted and reviewed by Reliability
Cross-team cutover checklist signed off by PM, ENG leads, and Design where applicable

notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: smaller initial canary reduces blast radius but delays detection of scale-related regressions. Chose a 2-stage approach to balance safety and speed.
Tradeoff: reserving larger burst capacity increases monthly committed spend; finance approved baseline reserving with elastic burst tied to cloud credits for first 30 days.
Decision: Start with eu-west-3 and ap-southeast-1 for pilot regions to cover latency-sensitive EU customers and APAC growth; US regions follow in second wave.
Open risk: kernel scheduling edge-case at high concurrency noted by runtime team; mitigations include reduced concurrency cap during initial 48 hours and kernel patch tracked in ENG-5123.
